system.name: Agentic Request to Fulfill (example)
system.description: Illustrative example. An employee asks internal IT for access, equipment, or a standard change, and the process fulfills the request or refuses it. Incident to Resolution tracks a customer-reported product or service break and the customer notice. Request to Fulfill changes an internal entitlement or completes an internal request. An orchestration agent and five sub-agents run on a reasoning LLM from an AI Model Provider. Hard rules (no self-approval, privilege caps, a production change window, and segregation of duties) are enforced by a policy service outside the model. Entitlement is scored by a separate component that is not on the reasoning-LLM path. Every owner is a placeholder.

L1 owner is named as the change approver for model settings
Log rule version, inputs, decision and authority for each request
Agent context limited to one requester at a time

Production changes outside the window blocked until the exception is approved

threats.title: A crafted request makes the intake agent open a ticket for the wrong worker

risk.failure_mode: Untrusted request text treated as a verified claim
risk.impact: A request is opened on another worker's identity

threats.title: Unapproved edit to the orchestration logic skips the entitlement score

risk.failure_mode: Step order changed without L1 approval
risk.impact: Fulfillment proceeds with no entitlement score

threats.title: Reasoning LLM reads 'the user is locked out' as permission to skip the approver

risk.failure_mode: A lockout note is read as a waiver of the approver rule
risk.impact: Privilege is granted with no approver

threats.catalog_note: No entry in /data/threats.json matches this threat. The catalog's model-behavior entries, such as evasion and prompt injection, assume an attacker. Here the model misreads plain business wording and no attacker is involved, so the threat is left unmapped.
threats.notes: Accountable: the AI Model Provider on the provider side (Bill, Nov 17, 2026), the same rule /data/threats.json uses for model-behavior threats. The hard rules stay in the policy service, outside the model.
